Event: `487561933eb032da859906b0adbf46d1` · 2026-09-24T23:11:35Z

> K6 plan v1 (PLAN ONLY). Plan file: ~/.claude/plans/wash-inbox-1-message-sorted-rocket.md
> Planned against wp-k5 at 1c5d3b324 (read-only) plus the approved K5b plan. Implemented only after K5 and K5b merge; commit 0 re-greps every inventory. Posted in 4 parts: [part 1/4] ODs, [2/4] inventory, [3/4] kernel, abi, ratchet, model, [4/4] tests, commits, risks, questions.
> 
> [part 1/4] OWNER DECISIONS (each with a recommendation)
> 
> OD1. Hosted arch: DELETE (recommended). Goes: kernel/src/arch/hosted (~1,050 lines), kernel/src/test.rs (1,258, every test drives the legacy interface), every cfg(not(baremetal)) / any(windows,unix) / all(ci,test) branch (~180 sites), the host-only deps (crossbeam-channel, hex, lazy_static, rand, the processes-as-threads dev-dep), and libs/abi's hosted/test/arm backends (~1,700). The kernel becomes no_std/no_main unconditionally, as the loader already is. Why: 112 errors, not in the bench, and it tests only calls K6 deletes; the model, the QEMU bench (both widths) and C1 replay cover it. Alternative: repair means porting it to the Redoubt calls, a new L-size package outside K6.
> 
> OD2. Test fixture after SIDs (log-server serves ~40 cases through a SID today). Recommended:
> (a) An INTERIM log endpoint in the kernel's boot wiring (budget.rs, beside boot_endpoint). The first program gets the receive right, after its device handles; every later program gets a send handle in slot 2, badged with its PID (slot 1 stays the boot endpoint). ~20 kernel lines; R3 removes it.
> (b) log-server is the FIRST program of every case that uses it, so it holds the console MMIO and IRQ handles, Reset and root/system/users.
>   - It relays with the kernel-minted badge as the [pid N] prefix. A badged handle cannot mint another badge, so the prefix is unforgeable.
>   - TAKE_BUDGETS: its reply moves root/system/users to the first caller, so the budget attackers stay away from the console.
>   - POWEROFF: it prints the fixed line '[server] power-off asked by pid N', then system_reset. Attack cases expect the checker's PID there, so an early power-off by an attacker is visible and fails the case.
> (c) Non-attack cases whose test program comes first today (redoubt-dead, redoubt-revoke, redoubt-tight, ipc-outcomes, budget-test, budget-mem-churn) print through the console handle directly, via one shared test_programs::console helper (the proc-test/sched.rs pattern), and drop log-server.
> Rejected: give the console to a bench-named program (grants under another name); let the attacker-first program hand the console to log-server (it could keep a mapping and forge verdict lines).
> 
> OD3. Keep NUMBER_BASE = 0x100 (recommended). Every a0 below it is an unknown number: InvalidArgument at decoding, in the Redoubt encoding (KERNEL-SPEC Errors, stage 1). Setting it to 0 renumbers every call, churning redoubt-sys, rt, model traces and fuzz seeds for no gain, and loses the clean 'old numbers stay dead' test.
> 
> OD4. libs/abi: strip it, move the kernel's internal Error into the kernel, rename the crate redoubt-layout (recommended). Keeps: the riscv layout constants and physmap helpers, PID/TID, MemoryFlags, MemoryRange/Address/Size, MemoryType. The legacy-numbered Error becomes kernel-private (kernel/src/kerr.rs); after K6 no value of it can reach a user register, since the legacy return path is gone. The rename is one mechanical final commit and can be deferred. Folding kernel-internal errors into redoubt_sys::Error is NOT in K6 (the spec fixes the error order; too risky mechanically): ASTRA follow-up.
> 
> OD5. Unsafe baseline 'before WP-K1': count like for like (recommended). The pre-K1 ceilings (d9c9be99a) summed to 88, but left out 9 existing kernel sites (cell, debug, smp, physmap; G1 added them later) and the whole legacy ABI. Same method on both trees: pre-K1 kernel 58 vs 51 today; legacy ABI 52 vs 52; loader 17/17; paging 12/12. K6 targets: kernel ceilings <= 50 in total (that includes K5b's window, ~+2; below both 58 and today's 54); abi/layout <= 6, 0 undocumented; the whole ratchet ~151 -> ~103, below every pre-K1 reading. The implementer runs the bench's checker on the pre-K1 tree and on the result and reports both. A strict reading (below the pre-K1 kernel ceiling of 49) would also need kmain's self-ecall replaced by a direct context switch (OD7): not recommended inside K6.
> 
> OD6. Demand paging stays only for loader-program stacks, INTERIM until R3 (recommended). After K6 no user call can create a reservation (MapMemory phys=0 and IncreaseHeap both go). reserve_range, the fault path ensure_page_exists_inner and ensure_range_exists serve only the loader programs' starting stacks. Eager backing (~32 pages per program, charged to system; touches the Q115 wording) belongs to R3, which ends loader-started programs.
> 
> OD7. kmain's switch stays a self-ecall, on an S-mode-only private path (recommended). The CallFromSMode trap arm takes (pid, tid) for kmain, its only S-mode caller; every CallFromUMode goes to redoubt::handle, whatever a0 is. SWITCHTO_CALLER, ORIGINAL_PID/TID and do_yield's parent logic move from syscall.rs to sched.rs. A direct context switch without a trap is deferred (new asm, new risk).
> 
> OD8. Tests deleted because their bug class disappears: grant-attack, grant-pid-reuse (with grant-donor and grant-reuse), callback-state-attack, and syscall-attack's heap half. The new legacy-gone case replaces them. Everything else is migrated, not deleted.
> 
> Context: K6 leaves exactly one syscall decoder facing userspace. It also closes two residuals K5 left until K6: a callback that never returns holds the CPU and every deadline; and legacy direct switches (borrowed quanta) run a budget no pick chose, which the model lacks.

Event: `ef40fa152ee24524182a2e2856a233af` · 2026-09-24T23:14:06Z

> Rulings folded into the plan file (v1.1). Two additions:
> 
> 1. OD2, the log badge is attribution only, never authority (new sub-bullet):
> - log-server grants nothing by badge value. TAKE_BUDGETS is first-come, and POWEROFF only names its caller in a fixed line; holding the handle is what allows the call, and the badge only labels the line.
> - The kernel writes the badge once, at boot, for the loader programs. A process that process_create later gives a reused PID receives no log handle and so no badge, because the boot wiring never runs again. It can only log through a handle its parent chooses to pass, carrying the parent's badge.
> - log-server holds the receive right but never mints, so no second badge exists.
> - The pid-reuse-authority case asserts that a reused PID holds no log handle.
> - The log endpoint is INTERIM and goes away when R3's init owns the console and hands out logging handles from the manifest.
> 
> 2. New Redoubt-interface guard, pid-reuse-authority (boot; rv64 and rv32; debug assertions), landing in commit 5 with the grant-pid-reuse deletion. Existing coverage does not do this: process-lifecycle asserts only reuse|=seen[pid] plus exact budgets (proc-lifecycle.rs:206-222), and proc-attack only 'permits reuse'; neither checks authority.
> The case: one first-in-bundle program (direct console, spawn.rs) starts child A with a send handle to its endpoint E minted with badge 7, its own exit endpoint, the console IRQ handle, a non-console device handle and a budget handle. A holds an open call on E, maps the device, and exits with calls pending. The parent then spawns until child B receives A's PID. B's handle list is empty except for a fresh badge-9 endpoint. Assertions:
> (a) every index 1..=64 but that one is BadHandle, probed with budget_usage, map_device, receive and handle_close;
> (b) no mapping at A's device address (a grandchild's read faults) and no log handle;
> (c) B's message arrives with badge 9, never 7;
> (d) the parent receives only B's own notices, and A's abandoned-call notice, which went to E's receiver before B existed, is not repeated to B;
> (e) the IRQ object stays the parent's: after B's 'up' line the bench types a byte ([[input]]), the parent's receive wakes, and B gets nothing.
> It can merge into proc-attack if the reviewer prefers.
> 
> K6-d3 and K6-k5b are noted as ruled. Nothing else changed; the red review can proceed on v1.1.

> 1. redoubt-layout (the stripped libs/abi) keeps only what the kernel and loader genuinely share and nothing user-facing. Remove every type or constant that duplicates redoubt-sys (e.g. MemoryFlags vs redoubt_sys MemFlags, address and size types, page constants): ONE definition each. If redoubt-sys already owns it, the kernel and loader use redoubt-sys's, or redoubt-sys re-exports redoubt-layout's; pick the direction that leaves no duplication.
